title: Elephant Fan
paragraphs: Anyway, putting what happened later aside, this took place on the way home.
“Waaaaaah…”
In the town of Siltvelt, a squirrel-like Beastman child was walking around, crying and looking around as if searching for something.
“What’s wrong?”
Kou transformed into an angel right then and there and called out to the squirrel-like Beastman child.
“…I got lost. Where am I? I want to see my mom.”
“Um… where did you get separated from her?”
“The shopping district.”
“Then let’s look for her together, okay?”
The squirrel-like Beastman child nodded in agreement at Kou’s suggestion.
“Hold still for a sec—”
Kou tucked his head under the squirrel-like Beastman’s legs and gave a mighty heave to stand up.
“Whoa! That’s amazing! You’re so strong!”
“Yep. Kou’s strong! So, do you think we’ll find your mom?”
“Huh? Hmm… I can’t see her.”
“Then let’s go this way. Kitamura, come on!”
“Got it! Where could this kid’s mom be? She’s lost!”
And so, we made our way through the shopping district, searching for the lost child’s parent. However, far from finding the child’s parent, we end up getting swept up in the lively crowd.
“Hmm… Hey, this might surprise you a bit, but please don’t struggle—it’s dangerous.”
“Huh? Okay.”

Kou gently explains the situation to the lost child, and after getting their consent, he transforms into the Filolial King. With a “puff,” he changes form, startling those around him. Though in Siltvelt, where there are many Beastmen and others who can transform, people don’t seem all that surprised. Still, combined with his striking height, Kou now stands out even in the crowd.
“Is anyone here this child’s mom?”
“Here, right here!”
I can see a hand raised somewhere in the crowd.
“Ah! It’s her mom!”
And just like that, the lost child’s parent was found in a flash.
“I’m truly sorry for the trouble.”
The Beastman, the child’s parent, bows to me—Kou’s guardian. Since everyone in the kingdom knows I’m the Spear Hero, she was so surprised she nearly fell over.
“I’m glad nothing serious happened.”
“That’s a relief.”
“Thanks a lot!”
“W-well then… I’ll repay you someday.”
“Don’t worry about it.”
“Well then.”
And so, we waved goodbye to the squirrel Beastman and his child and left the scene.
“Hum, hum…”
Kou walks along the path back to the castle, humming to himself. But… seeing that exchange just now, I’m really happy that Kou has grown into such a kind-hearted child.
Suddenly, the image of Kou—who had been fiercely scolded by Father after suggesting he wanted to eat a Mole—flashed through my mind.
That’s right. There’s a terrifying incident here that haunts Kou’s psyche. Without Big Sister or her friends around, Kou would probably start saying he wants to eat little Beastmen.
“Kou.”
“What?”
“Why did you approach that lost child just now?”
“Huh? Was that a bad idea?”
“No, I think you did a very good thing, Kou. But I asked because I wondered if you’d approached him just because he looked tasty.”
At that, Kou furrowed his brow, looking slightly annoyed.
“Eh—I wouldn’t eat him! Kou isn’t that much of a glutton.”

Oh, this is trauma avoidance. It’s safe to assume he’s no longer in danger of punishment from Father. But how did things turn out this way? Could it be that it’s already too late…? Maybe he’s already been punished by Father without me knowing.
“Oh, but the old Kou might have thought about it—maybe.”
“Is that so?”
“Yeah. Elmero—you see, when I was looking at the little Beastmen in the castle and thinking they looked delicious, he taught me that I shouldn’t eat them.”
What?! So that elephant stepped in for Big Sisters!? I knew they got along well, but this is quite a revelation.
“That’s good to hear.”
“Yeah!”
And so, we returned to the castle.
After that, I casually observed Zou playing with—not Kou, but—Filolial-sama and the others.
“Alright, everyone—let’s get our pitches in sync first—”
There he was, holding a conductor’s baton and teaching the gathered Filolial-samas how to sing in harmony.
“Ah…”
“Okay. Let’s sing again!”
“Okay!”
“Whoa!”
It certainly seemed like he was teaching them music thoroughly and with joy. A lively harmony echoed through the castle. Such pleasant singing voices.

I see. I’ve been pretty busy myself, so I hadn’t checked on things, but this is what’s been going on, then. It’s wonderful. Thanks to this elephant’s lessons, Filolial-sama and the others have naturally been improving their skills as idols. Since I don’t teach opera-style singing myself, this is great practice.
“Alright, that’s all for today.”
“Okayyy!”
“See you tomorrow!”
“See you tomorrow!”
I watch as Zou wraps up his fun singing session, says goodbye to Filolial-sama and the others, and heads back into the castle.
“Zou.”
“Huh? Oh, Spear Hero. Hello.”
When I called out to Zou, he greeted me in return.
“Not only did you teach Kou all sorts of things, but you were also teaching Filolial-sama and the others how to sing, weren’t you? Thank you very much for doing that.”
“Ah, yes.”
If he’s this capable, I suppose I’ll have to do my part to help him out as well. A favor for a favor, after all.
“As a token of my gratitude, I’ll allow you to get along better with Father from now on.”
“Ah, thank you…?”
It seemed Panda was trying to win over Father by positioning himself as someone he could rely on, but let’s push Zou a little more toward Father.
“Um… Why are you giving me permission, Spear Hero?”

Zou is tilting his head in confusion. Well, it’s only natural that he’d feel awkward about me meddling in Father’s love life. But as Father’s loyal subordinate, I want him to choose his partner wisely. Specifically…
“You must protect Father from Rival advances and win his heart.”
“Uh, uh-huh…”
“I’m rooting for you, too.”
Zou listened to me, looking as if he didn’t quite get it.
That evening, at the dinner table. Thanks to Father’s suggestion, we were all enjoying a pleasant meal together. Today, on a whim, Father had prepared a special meal just for us.
“Yum!”
“Hmm… Though we rarely get to eat it, Lord Iwatani’s cooking is truly exquisite.”
Sakura-chan and Éclair are both raving about Father’s cooking. Of course, Yuki-chan, Kou, and I feel the same way.
“Thank you. I saw something interesting on the menu for lunch today, so I tried recreating it to suit everyone’s tastes—what did you think?”
“I guess I can’t feed this to the chef… in a cruel way.”
“I think it’s delicious.”
Even Panda and Elephant are honest about Father’s cooking. By the way, Rival has work at Shieldfreeden tonight and can’t make it. Father was worried about that, but there’s no need to be.
“Ah, that’s right. Father, I’d like to have a word with you.”
“What is it, Motoyasu-kun?”
“Father, getting along with Panda is all well and good, but Zou isn’t so bad either. This guy’s a good Zou.”
“W-Wait, the Spear Hero…!?”

The elephant is looking at me with a somewhat troubled expression, but he’s just trying to be humble, isn’t he? I’m not oblivious! People—pigs, to be exact—have often called me oblivious or stupid, but that’s not true! Motoyasu, the capable man… I’ll make sure to show Father right here just how outstanding this elephant is. This is my way of thanking Zou for getting along so well with Filolial-sama and the others from the very beginning!
“Hm? I’m not quite sure what you mean—are you talking about Elmero-san?”
“That’s right!”
“I’m starting to think it might be time for Motoyasu-kun to stop calling Elmero-san ‘Zou,’ don’t you think?”
“Hmm? Is that so?”
“I wonder how much longer you’re going to call me ‘Panda’…”
“A panda is a panda. Just as an Éclair is an Éclair, you see.”
“No, it’s just that Lord Kitamura keeps calling me the wrong name, but my name is Éclair…”
Éclair seems to be protesting about something.
“Éclair is Éclair, after all.”

“…I’ve realized it’s easier for me not to worry about it, so please don’t make a big deal out of it. Just being recognized by Lord Kitamura as a human woman sets me apart from the rest. It would be a mistake to expect too much.”
“Ah… yeah. Besides, Lars-chan has transformed into a Beastman form too, just to make it easier to talk.”
“I was surprised that when I spoke to her in her Demi-Human form, she acted like she wasn’t even listening… In that sense, isn’t she kind of rare?”
Did something strange happen? Anyway, I’m Zou. Since we’re connected through Kou, I’ll try my best to remember your names.
“Um… was it Melon?”
Zou immediately denied it. Looks like I got it wrong.
“Just like with Eclair-san, why are they all dessert-themed…?”
Hmm, I’m pretty sure the name was something like that. Something like “Elmelon,” I think.
“Motoyasu-kun, who’s been getting called by all sorts of names this whole time but just remembers them haphazardly…”
“Actually, the fact that only Elmero is being called by his proper name by the Spear Hero here is kind of—”
“Panda, you’re being too picky. It’s because Melon is a good Zou.”
“Please, really, stop it…”
Melon seems troubled. I’m not trying to trouble Melon… I mean, the elephant. I just want to repay the favor he did me by guiding Kou.
“It’s a hassle for me too, so I’ll just let them call me whatever they want. I mean… by that logic, I think we’d have to call the Knights of Melromarc ‘humans,’ don’t you think?”
“I’m not exactly being called by my correct name either, though…”
“Now, now… So, what’s up with Elmero?”
After mediating like that, Father asked me about Zou.
“As I was saying, Zou is a good Zou.”
“Yeah, that’s true. He’s serious, and he helps mediate between Eclair and Lars-chan, so he’s been a big help.”
“But that’s not all!”
I explained Kou’s problem to Father.
“Filolials are actually surprisingly dangerous creatures, you know…”
For some reason, Panda said this with a distant look in his eyes. What’s that about!? Does he have a complaint against Filolial-sama or something?
“I can’t deny it. Before meeting you heroes, I thought they were gentle creatures…”
Even Éclair agrees. Father is giving a wry smile.
“Hmm? Did Kou do something wrong?”
“No, I didn’t.”
“That’s right. I think Kou did something really good.”
Kou looks a little embarrassed after being praised by me and Father.
“Ehehe…”
“It’s just… I’ve heard there’s a Kou who went through a very scary experience.”
“So there’s that much of a difference, huh… I wonder if Gaelion-chan knows about it?”
I did wonder why a Rival had to come up at that moment, but since she’s stuck in the same loop as me, she probably just wants to hear a different perspective.
“You’re welcome to ask him when I’m not around.”
I wouldn’t be happy hearing it from Rival’s mouth, after all. But it’s a problem that definitely exists as a fact.
“Hmm?”
Sakura-chan is tilting her head, looking like she doesn’t quite understand.
“What’s Naofumi like when he gets angry? Like when there was poison in the castle?”
“That wasn’t really that scary, was it?”
“That’s true. It’s hard to imagine. Maybe like that high-pressure vibe at Shieldfreeden?”

Kou and Yuki-chan don’t seem to get it either. I knew it, I knew it. Even that Father from the loop didn’t get angry just for the sake of it. He steeled his heart and scolded Kou because he had Kou’s best interests at heart. So it’s only natural to be scared.
“That would have been such a terrifying experience that Kou would have become a coward.”
“Boo! Kou isn’t scared!”
“Kou, since Motoyasu-sama says so, it must be true. You should be glad you managed to avoid that.”
“It really doesn’t quite click, though. Especially considering how you usually act. Did you even jump on my back or anything?”
“Well, I try not to get angry too much myself, and as for that incident at Shieldfreeden, I only did what I had to because I had to be firm. That was… um, a bit mentally draining.”
Father seemed pretty worn out back then, too. I can’t compete with Filolial-sama’s noble feathers, but pandas do have really fluffy fur, after all.
“Iwatani isn’t scary, is he?”
“I’ve heard there are even some Kous who are afraid of him.”
“Boo! Kou isn’t afraid of anything!”
I suppose that’s just because Kou’s a boy. It feels like he’s arguing back because someone pointed out a weakness he hasn’t experienced yet.
“That said, you mustn’t make Father angry! It’s irreversible! Shh!”
You mustn’t traumatize Kou by saying the wrong thing! But thanks to Zou, we can rest easy now.
